subject: mathematics

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.112, chapter 10 INVERSE TRIGONOMETRIC FUNCTIONS, Short Answer question 2(i). Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The split is 1+1+1+1 because the four moves are genuinely separate pieces of work — naming the angles, doubling one of them, expanding the difference, and proving the result lies in the range of Cos⁻¹. NOTATION: the book prints the inverse functions in lower case (sin⁻¹, cos⁻¹); they are written here with capitals to match the principal-value convention used across the rest of this unit. Both sides were checked numerically to twelve decimal places: 2·arcsin(0.6) − arccos(5/13) = arccos(323/325) = 0.110997010491. Paper position: Maths-1A Section B prints eight short answers of which the student writes any six, at 4 marks each, under the 2026-27 pattern; Inverse Trigonometric Functions is an SAQ-only unit, so the paper gives it no Section-A and no Section-C slot. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this — name each move in order, and say which formula you reach for and why.

steps.label: Name the two angles
steps.margin_note: First mark. Naming the angles turns the statement into cos(2A − B) = 323/325, which is a plain expansion.
steps.memory_tip: 3-4-5 and 5-12-13 are the two triangles here. Write all four ratios before starting.

recall.must_convey: That A and B are named as first-quadrant angles with all four ratios written down.
accept: let a be sin inverse three fifths and b be cos inverse five thirteenths, then write all four ratios
both angles are first quadrant so every ratio is positive
cos a is four fifths and sin b is twelve thirteenths
rendu angles ki peru pettali, four ratios rasali
name the angles and use the three four five and five twelve thirteen triangles

steps.why: Both inverse values are positive, so A and B are first-quadrant angles. Every sine and cosine below is then a positive number.
common_mistakes: Reading Sin⁻¹(3/5) as an angle whose cosine is 3/5.

steps.label: Double the first angle
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Both double-angle values are needed, because the expansion of cos(2A − B) uses each one.
steps.memory_tip: cos2A = 1 − 2sin²A takes sinA straight in; sin2A = 2 sinA cosA needs both ratios.

recall.must_convey: That cos2A = 7/25 and sin2A = 24/25 are computed from the double-angle formulas.
accept: use one minus two sine squared to get cos two a as seven over twenty five
sin two a is two sin a cos a which is twenty four over twenty five
find both double angle values first
cos two a seven by twenty five, sin two a twenty four by twenty five
double the first angle before subtracting

steps.why: The statement has 2A, not A, so both double-angle values are needed before any subtraction can be written.
common_mistakes: Using cos2A = 2cos²A − 1 with sinA by mistake.

steps.label: Expand cos of the difference
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Both products already sit over 325, so they add with no extra work.
steps.memory_tip: cos(X − Y) = cosX cosY + sinX sinY — the sign turns to plus for a difference.
lines: cos(2A − B) = cos2A cosB + sin2A sinB

recall.must_convey: That cos(2A − B) is expanded with a plus sign and comes to 323/325.
accept: expand cos of two a minus b as cos cos plus sin sin
the two products are thirty five over three twenty five and two eighty eight over three twenty five
they add to three twenty three over three twenty five
cos difference lo plus sign vasthundi, three twenty three by three twenty five
the cosine of the difference is three twenty three by three twenty five

steps.why: The difference formula for cosine carries a plus sign between the two products. That sign is what produces 323 and not 253.
common_mistakes: Writing a minus sign between the two products.
Using the sine difference formula instead.

steps.label: Check the range and close
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Cosine decreases as the angle increases on (0, π), so the smaller cosine 7/25 belongs to the bigger angle — that is how 2A > B is proved.
steps.memory_tip: Cos⁻¹ only returns angles in [0, π]. Show 2A − B is positive and below π before writing the last line.
lines: This is inside [0, π], the range of Cos⁻¹.

recall.must_convey: That 2A − B is shown to lie in [0, π] before it is written as Cos⁻¹(323/325).
accept: show two a minus b is positive and less than pi so it is inside the range of cos inverse
the smaller cosine belongs to the bigger angle so two a is greater than b
the angle is in the first quadrant so we can write it as cos inverse
range check cheyyali, appude cos inverse rayochu
since the difference lies in zero to pi the result follows
reject: the two products add to three twenty three
heard_as: cos inverse three twenty three by three twenty five

steps.why: Knowing the cosine is not enough. Cos⁻¹ returns a value in [0, π], so the angle 2A − B must be shown to lie there before it can be written as Cos⁻¹(323/325).
common_mistakes: Writing the Cos⁻¹ line without checking the range.
Assuming 2A > B with no reason given.
